_: Little Big Questions: How is a volcano born? Free narration (Kokoro, sound.yml) and the free score. Words exactly as the vo lines; facts in docs/research/KIDS_FACTS_2026-10.md.

vo.text: Deep under our feet, it is so hot that rock can melt.
This melted rock is called magma. It is lighter than the rock around it, so it slowly pushes up, and up.
It finds a crack. The pressure builds. The ground begins to rumble.
And then, whoosh! It bursts out of the ground. Now we call it lava.
The lava cools down, and turns into brand new rock.
Every time it erupts, it adds another layer, and the mountain grows taller and taller.
When the volcano rests, rain and sun make the land green again. Volcano soil is wonderful for growing plants.
Some islands, like the islands of Hawaii, were built by volcanoes, one eruption at a time.
So the ground under your feet is not as still as it looks.
